# Togakushi ⇆ Nagano


Togakushi – Nagano Sightseeing Bus (Starts from April 1, 2025)


- To ensure passenger safety and comfort, **all seats require a reservation**. You don’t have to worry about not getting a seat due to full capacity.
- You can store your suitcases and large luggage in the trunk room.
- You can ride without a reservation if there are empty seats, but booking in advance lets you board smoothly without waiting in line. You can pay the fare on the bus using **contactless-enabled** **VISA cards or cash**.
- Some bus stops arefor boarding only or drop-off only. Please check the timetable carefully.
- IC cards like SUICA cannot be used on this bus.
- Please note that the Togakushi & Zenkoji 1-Day Pass will be discontinued as of April 1, 2025.
- On the bus from Togakushi to Nagano, you may board at a different stop on the same reserved bus as long as the fare does not change. However, even if there are seats available, you cannot use your reserved ticket for a different bus. Please cancel your reservation before the cancellation deadline and make a new booking. (The cancellation deadline is printed on your ticket.)
- For travel within the Togakushi area, please use the [Togakushi Shuttle Bus](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/timetable/togakushi-shuttlebus?hsLang=en).
- Bus number 73 is no longer in service.
- Bus number 70 is a dedicated, non-reserved service primarily intended for local residents of Togakushi. For tourists, please use the reserved Nagano–Togakushi bus, which is shown on this page.

### Important Info

![reservation-error-icon](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/images/icon/reservation-error-icon.png?width=500&height=500&name=reservation-error-icon.png)Troubles while making a reservation online

- Alpico does not handle the operation of the reservation website. If you encounter issues like your card being denied, the reservation page loading slowly, not sure what to fill in the form, error occuring while proceeding, or being unable to proceed despite availability, etc., please reach out to Keio Dentetsu, which is the company that manages the reservation website, directly at [info@highwaybus.com](mailto:info@highwaybus.com) for help.
- We often receive inquiries about card denials, but when we test it, it usually works fine. So, please try using other cards or attempt booking later the next day or contact your card issuer.
- When making a reservation online, if your country phone number has less than 9 digits, add a 0 at the beginning to meet the requirement (9-11 digits).
- If you don’t see the bus you want to book on the booking website,it means that bus is full. Please choose another available bus.
- The online reservation system and the ticket counter share the same seat availability.If online bookings show no available seats, the ticket counter will have the same status.
- To check seat availability for the reserved bus, please visit the reservation page. If the bus is fully booked, you will see indicators such as “×”, “No Seat Available”, or “Not Available”. We will not answer to the inquiries about the seat availability.
- When making a reservation, please check this box (reCAPTCHA) to proceed with your booking.

![i-am-not-robot](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/i-am-not-robot.png?width=439&height=184&name=i-am-not-robot.png)
- When making a reservation, to reverse the route direction, please click the button below.



![route_diverse](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/route_diverse.png?width=990&height=173&name=route_diverse.png)


![ticketing-icon](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/images/icon/ticketing-icon.png?width=500&height=500&name=ticketing-icon.png)Ticket Reservation / Cancellation / Change

##### **Ticket Reservation**

- Please make a reservation by yourself. We do not accept reservation requests, regardless of the number of passengers or requests from travel agencies.
- The online reservation system and the ticket counter share the same seat availability.If online bookings show no available seats, the ticket counter will have the same status.
- If you encounter any issues while making a reservation, please contact [info@highwaybus.com](mailto:info@highwaybus.com) or use the [Contact Form](https://japantripsearch.com/). Alpico does not manage the reservation system.

##### **Ticket Cancellation**

- Please access " [My Reservation](https://www.highwaybus.com/gp/inbound/inbRsvSearch)" page and proceed with the reservation cancellation.
- If you cannot log into "My Reservation" page, please contact [info@highwaybus.com](mailto:info@highwaybus.com) or use the [Contact Form](https://japantripsearch.com/). Alpico does not manage the reservation system.
- Cancellation fee applies 100 yen per person.

##### **Ticket Change**

- You cannot change your reservation information (time/date/name etc.). Please cancel and make a new reservation by yourself online from [this page](https://japanbusonline.com/en/BookInquiry).
- If you cannot log into "My Reservation" page, please contact [info@highwaybus.com](mailto:info@highwaybus.com) or use the [Contact Form](https://japantripsearch.com/). Alpico does not manage the reservation system.
- Cancellation fee applies 100 yen per person.

![bus-location-icon](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/images/icon/bus-location-icon.png?width=500&height=500&name=bus-location-icon.png)How to Board the Bus

- **Boarding Location**

Please board the bus from bus stop no. 7 near Nagano station Zenkoji exit.  The bus stop is in front of the Alpico Bus Ticket Office. ( [Google Map](https://www.google.com/maps/place/%E3%82%A2%E3%83%AB%E3%83%94%E3%82%B3%E4%BA%A4%E9%80%9A+%E9%95%B7%E9%87%8E%E9%A7%85%E5%89%8D%E6%A1%88%E5%86%85%E6%89%80/data=!4m2!3m1!1s0x0:0x299d8f3be9e631ca?sa=X&ved=1t:2428&ictx=111))

- **How to Board the Bus**

After purchasing tickets online, you can confirm and make changes to the ticket type from the " [My Reservation](https://www.highwaybus.com/gp/inbound/inbRsvSearch)" page. There are two types of online tickets.

**1\. Mobile Ticket (Recommended):**

Show the ticket on your smartphone screen when boarding.

- After completing your reservation and payment, click the **"Send Mobile Ticket"** button.
- A link to your mobile ticket will be sent to your registered email.
- If needed, you can log into the **"My Reservation"** page and click **"Send Mobile Ticket"** again to resend the ticket.

**2\. Web Ticket:**

Print out the ticket and show it to the bus staff or driver when boarding.

- After purchasing a ticket online, click the **"Display/Print Web Ticket"** button.
- This will open the ticket for you to print.
- If needed, you can log into the **"My Reservation"** page and click " **Display/Print Web Ticket"** button again to resend the ticket.

[Detailed Instructions with Illustrations on How to Receive Your Ticket >](https://highway-buses.jp/boarding)

[See how to board the bus (video) >](https://highway-buses.jp/movie/boarding/en.mp4)

If you cannot log into your reservation page, please contact Highwaybus.com directly:

- Email: [info@highwaybus.com](mailto:info@highwaybus.com)
- Inquiry form: [http://japantripsearch.com](http://japantripsearch.com/)

- We typically update the timetable for the green season around mid-March and for the winter season around late November.
- If the new schedule is not yet available, we kindly ask for your patience. Please refrain from inquiring about the release date, as we cannot offer additional details beyond what is provided on the timetable page.
- This bus service operates year-round, with only minor changes to the schedule compared to last year. Until the updated timetable is released, you may refer to last year's schedule as a guide.

![luggage-icon](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/images/icon/luggage-icon.png?width=500&height=500&name=luggage-icon.png)Luggage Allowance

- This bus has a luggage compartment where you can stow your suitcases. There are no restrictions on the number or size of items.
- However, we do not take any responsibility for any damage to your belongings.

![toilet-icon](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/images/icon/toilet-icon.png?width=500&height=500&name=toilet-icon.png)Onboard Facilities

- This bus does not have a restroom onboard, and there are no restroom breaks during the journey.
- This bus is not equipped with a wheelchair lift or designated wheelchair space, so it cannot accommodate passengers who wish to remain in their wheelchair during the journey. Please fold your wheelchair and store it in the bus's luggage compartment. Kindly note that unfolded wheelchairs cannot be accepted.

### Fare

- Only one-way tickets are available; there is no round-trip fare.

|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nagano Station ～ Togakushi Area | Adult | 2,500 yen |
| Nagano Station ～ Iizuna Kogen / Nagano Forest Village | Adult | 1,500 yen |

##### Children’s fares

- **Age 0:** Free of charge
- **Age 1-6:** For legal and safety reasons, it is **recommended** that children in this age group have a reserved child fare seat. Please check the booking site for the exact fare.
- **Age 7-12:** Child fare(Please confirm the exact child fare on the reservation website.)
- **Age 13+:** Adult Fare

※By law, children and infants who do not occupy a seat (e.g., sitting on a parent’s lap) are also counted as passengers. If a child does not have a reserved seat when the bus is fully booked, this will be considered over capacity and boarding may be denied. Therefore, we recommend reserving a seat for your child and infant, even if they do not intend to use it.

※ Alpico does not operate its own reservation websites. Similar to hotel booking sites, bus tickets are sold through third-party reservation platforms such as [japanbusonline.com](https://japanbusonline.com/) or [highwaybus.com](https://www.highwaybus.com/gp/inbound/index). If there is any discrepancy between the child fare categories shown on the reservation site and those stated on this page, the information on this page takes priority.

# Togakushi ⇆ Nagano


Togakushi – Nagano Sightseeing Bus (Starts from April 1, 2025)


- Starting from December 6, 2025, this winter bus will make a stop at the Okusha Tokusha Bus Stop, the entrance to the ancient cedar tree path. From the bus stop, it takes about a 20-minute walk to the red Zuishinmon Gate.
- To ensure passenger safety and comfort, **all seats require a reservation**. You don’t have to worry about not getting a seat due to full capacity.
- You can store your suitcases and large luggage in the trunk room.
- You can ride without a reservation if there are empty seats, but booking in advance lets you board smoothly without waiting in line. You can pay the fare on the bus using **contactless-enabled** **VISA cards or cash**.
- Some bus stops arefor boarding only or drop-off only. Please check the timetable carefully.
- IC cards like SUICA cannot be used on this bus.
- Please note that the Togakushi & Zenkoji 1-Day Pass will be discontinued as of April 1, 2025.
- On the bus from Togakushi to Nagano, you may board at a different stop on the same reserved bus as long as the fare does not change. However, even if there are seats available, you cannot use your reserved ticket for a different bus. Please cancel your reservation before the cancellation deadline and make a new booking. (The cancellation deadline is printed on your ticket.)

- Bus number 73 is no longer in service.
- Bus number 70 is a dedicated, non-reserved service primarily intended for local residents of Togakushi. For tourists, please use the reserved Nagano–Togakushi bus, which is shown on this page.

### Important Info

![reservation-error-icon](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/images/icon/reservation-error-icon.png?width=500&height=500&name=reservation-error-icon.png)Troubles while making a reservation online

- Alpico does not handle the operation of the reservation website. If you encounter issues like your card being denied, the reservation page loading slowly, not sure what to fill in the form, error occuring while proceeding, or being unable to proceed despite availability, etc., please reach out to Keio Dentetsu, which is the company that manages the reservation website, directly at [info@highwaybus.com](mailto:info@highwaybus.com) for help.
- We often receive inquiries about card denials, but when we test it, it usually works fine. So, please try using other cards or attempt booking later the next day or contact your card issuer.
- When making a reservation online, if your country phone number has less than 9 digits, add a 0 at the beginning to meet the requirement (9-11 digits).
- If you don’t see the bus you want to book on the booking website,it means that bus is full. Please choose another available bus.
- The online reservation system and the ticket counter share the same seat availability.If online bookings show no available seats, the ticket counter will have the same status.
- To check seat availability for the reserved bus, please visit the reservation page. If the bus is fully booked, you will see indicators such as “×”, “No Seat Available”, or “Not Available”. We will not answer to the inquiries about the seat availability.
- When making a reservation, please check this box (reCAPTCHA) to proceed with your booking.

![i-am-not-robot](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/i-am-not-robot.png?width=439&height=184&name=i-am-not-robot.png)
- When making a reservation, to reverse the route direction, please click the button below.



![route_diverse](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/route_diverse.png?width=990&height=173&name=route_diverse.png)


![ticketing-icon](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/images/icon/ticketing-icon.png?width=500&height=500&name=ticketing-icon.png)Ticket Reservation / Cancellation / Change

##### **Ticket Reservation**

- Please make a reservation by yourself. We do not accept reservation requests, regardless of the number of passengers or requests from travel agencies.
- The online reservation system and the ticket counter share the same seat availability.If online bookings show no available seats, the ticket counter will have the same status.
- If you encounter any issues while making a reservation, please contact [info@highwaybus.com](mailto:info@highwaybus.com) or use the [Contact Form](https://japantripsearch.com/). Alpico does not manage the reservation system.

##### **Ticket Cancellation**

- Please access " [My Reservation](https://www.highwaybus.com/gp/inbound/inbRsvSearch)" page and proceed with the reservation cancellation.
- If you cannot log into "My Reservation" page, please contact [info@highwaybus.com](mailto:info@highwaybus.com) or use the [Contact Form](https://japantripsearch.com/). Alpico does not manage the reservation system.
- Cancellation fee applies 100 yen per person.

##### **Ticket Change**

- You cannot change your reservation information (time/date/name etc.). Please cancel and make a new reservation by yourself online from [this page](https://japanbusonline.com/en/BookInquiry).
- If you cannot log into "My Reservation" page, please contact [info@highwaybus.com](mailto:info@highwaybus.com) or use the [Contact Form](https://japantripsearch.com/). Alpico does not manage the reservation system.
- Cancellation fee applies 100 yen per person.

![bus-location-icon](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/images/icon/bus-location-icon.png?width=500&height=500&name=bus-location-icon.png)How to Board the Bus

- **Boarding Location**

Please board the bus from bus stop no. 7 near Nagano station Zenkoji exit.  The bus stop is in front of the Alpico Bus Ticket Office. ( [Google Map](https://www.google.com/maps/place/%E3%82%A2%E3%83%AB%E3%83%94%E3%82%B3%E4%BA%A4%E9%80%9A+%E9%95%B7%E9%87%8E%E9%A7%85%E5%89%8D%E6%A1%88%E5%86%85%E6%89%80/data=!4m2!3m1!1s0x0:0x299d8f3be9e631ca?sa=X&ved=1t:2428&ictx=111))

- **How to Board the Bus**

After purchasing tickets online, you can confirm and make changes to the ticket type from the " [My Reservation](https://www.highwaybus.com/gp/inbound/inbRsvSearch)" page. There are two types of online tickets.

**1\. Mobile Ticket (Recommended):**

Show the ticket on your smartphone screen when boarding.

- After completing your reservation and payment, click the **"Send Mobile Ticket"** button.
- A link to your mobile ticket will be sent to your registered email.
- If needed, you can log into the **"My Reservation"** page and click **"Send Mobile Ticket"** again to resend the ticket.

**2\. Web Ticket:**

Print out the ticket and show it to the bus staff or driver when boarding.

- After purchasing a ticket online, click the **"Display/Print Web Ticket"** button.
- This will open the ticket for you to print.
- If needed, you can log into the **"My Reservation"** page and click " **Display/Print Web Ticket"** button again to resend the ticket.

[Detailed Instructions with Illustrations on How to Receive Your Ticket >](https://highway-buses.jp/boarding)

[See how to board the bus (video) >](https://highway-buses.jp/movie/boarding/en.mp4)

If you cannot log into your reservation page, please contact Highwaybus.com directly:

- Email: [info@highwaybus.com](mailto:info@highwaybus.com)
- Inquiry form: [http://japantripsearch.com](http://japantripsearch.com/)

![timetable-icon](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/images/icon/timetable-icon.png?width=500&height=500&name=timetable-icon.png)Bus Timetable Updates

- **Age 0:** Free of charge

※By law, children and infants who do not occupy a seat (e.g., sitting on a parent’s lap) are also counted as passengers. If a child does not have a reserved seat when the bus is fully booked, this will be considered over capacity and boarding may be denied. Therefore, we recommend reserving a seat for your child and infant, even if they do not intend to use it.

※ Alpico does not operate its own reservation websites. Similar to hotel booking sites, bus tickets are sold through third-party reservation platforms such as [japanbusonline.com](https://japanbusonline.com/) or [highwaybus.com](https://www.highwaybus.com/gp/inbound/index). With this convenient ticket, you can explore the sacred Mt. Togakushi, the Zuishinmon Gate and cedar tree avenue, the serene Kagami Pond, and many other attractions in the Togakushi area at your own pace. This ticket provides unlimited rides for an entire day, allowing you to enjoy a relaxed and flexible journey. Additionally, it includes special discounts at select Togakushi soba restaurants. ## Coverage Areas and Routes ![where_map_en-1](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/images/Discount%20Tickets/Zenkoji_Togakushi%201-day%20Ticket/where_map_en-1.png?width=922&height=464&name=where_map_en-1.png) **(Select the tabs below to explore tourist attractions in the Togakushi and Nagano regions.)** - [1\. Ancient Cedar Avenue](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/tickets/zenkoji-togakushi-1day-ticket#) - [2\. Zenkoji Temple](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/tickets/zenkoji-togakushi-1day-ticket#) - [3\. Ninja Museum & Trick Mansion](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/tickets/zenkoji-togakushi-1day-ticket#) - [4\. Soba Museum](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/tickets/zenkoji-togakushi-1day-ticket#) - [5\. Chusha Shrine](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/tickets/zenkoji-togakushi-1day-ticket#) - [6\. Kagami Pond](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/tickets/zenkoji-togakushi-1day-ticket#) - [7\. Okusha Shrine](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/tickets/zenkoji-togakushi-1day-ticket#) ![mainvisual_img01_sp](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hubfs/images/Discount%20Tickets/Zenkoji_Togakushi%201-day%20Ticket/mainvisual_img01_sp.jpg) ![togakushi-1](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hubfs/images/travelog/articles/togakushi-1.jpg) What place? # Togakushi Travel Guide

[Area-Nagano City Area](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/tag/area-nagano-city-area) ,



[Outdoor Activities (Summer)](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/tag/outdoor-activities-summer) ,



[Temples and Shrines](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/tag/temples-and-shrines)

In the highlands above Nagano City is an ancient haunt of mountain ascetics. Take a walk through the forest, visit the many shrines scattered throughout and take in the majestic scenery of towering cedar trees and precipitous mountains. This is your guide to visiting Togakushi.

Updated: 2026-04-17

- [![LINE](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/images/icon-line-color.svg)](https://social-plugins.line.me/lineit/share?url=https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/togakushi-travel-guide)
- [![X](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/images/icon-x.svg)](http://twitter.com/share?text=Togakushi%20Travel%20Guide&url=https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/togakushi-travel-guide)

![ABG_2341](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_2341.jpg?width=1200&height=798&name=ABG_2341.jpg)

At the foot of Mt. Togakushi to the north of Nagano City, the lush forests of Togakushi are home to ancient shrines and picturesque scenery. Within its natural splendor lies a series of shrines connected by forest trails, with a breathtaking walk between 400-year-old cedar trees leading up to its final shrine.

Togakushi Travel Guide

- [Introduction](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/togakushi-travel-guide#page01)
- [Location and Access](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/togakushi-travel-guide#page02)

- [Things to do in Togakushi](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/togakushi-travel-guide#page04)
- [Nearby Sightseeing](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/togakushi-travel-guide#page05)
- [Where to Stay](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/togakushi-travel-guide#page06)

## Introduction

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_2304.jpg)A field of soba flowers with Mt. Togakushi in the background

The history of Togakushi is deeply rooted in Shinto mythology. According to legend, after the sun goddess Amaterasu had a fight with her younger brother, she hid herself in a cave and sealed the entrance with a massive rock. As a result, the world was plunged into pure darkness. All the other gods gathered together to form a plan to lure her out. The god of wisdom proposed holding a festival.  The dancing, frolicking and commotion got the attention of Amaterasu, and when she moved the boulder aside to take a peek, the god of strength picked up the rock and hurled it into the air—restoring light to the world.

The door was said to have fallen back down to Earth and landed in Nagano, becoming the precipitous mountain peaks of Togakushi. Fittingly, the name Togakushi comes from the characters 戸 (door) and 隠 (hidden), meaning “hidden door.”

## Location and Access

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/nagano-lp/togakushi-map.svg)

Togakushi sits high in the mountains above Nagano City and can be reached in around 45 to 75 minutes depending on mode of transport.

### By Bus

Direct buses bound for Togakushi depart from Nagano Station. From the Zenkoji Exit, cross the road towards the Don Quijote side and board the bus in front of the Alpico Bus Ticket Office at Bus Stop No. 7.

### By Car

The quickest and easiest way to visit Togakushi is by car. There are several car parks located near the shrines, with Okusha Shrine’s car park leading directly to the trailhead to Okusha Shrine and the rows of cedars. Paid parking is available at Okushairiguchi Parking Lot and is closest to the Okusha trail head. Other free and paid parking options are near the Chusha Shrine.

## When to Visit

Previous

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_2323.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_2323.jpg)

Kagami Pond in summer

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMGP8713.jpg?width=800&name=IMGP8713.jpg)

Fall foliage reflecting beautifully in Kagami Pond's water

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMGP6587.jpg?width=800&name=IMGP6587.jpg)

Trekking to Kagami Pond in winter with a Mt. Togakushi in the background

Next

- 1
- 2
- 3

Togakushi can be visited year-round but is especially popular during the summer months due to its cool climate and lush greenery. In autumn from to mid- to late October, the forests turn majestic shades of gold and orange, creating a dazzling spectacle around Kagami Pond and Togakushi’s many shrines.

### Winter in Togakushi

From late November to early April, many of Togakushi’s establishments close for winter. However, the heavy carpets of snow transform Togakushi into a winter wonderland, waiting to explored on snowshoes or cross-country skis.

Up until December of 2025, buses did not stop at the Togakushi Okusha bus stop during winter. The local Togakushi line still does not stop at Okusha, but the express bus does.

Regarding what to wear, warm winter clothes and waterproof boots with good grip are essential. Snow usually remains into mid- to late March.

## Things to do in Togakushi

### Walk the Five Shrines along the Togakushi Kodo Trail

Previous

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_2341.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_2341.jpg)

Zuijinmon Gate in front of the approach to Togakushi's famous cedar tree lane

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMGP6697.jpg?width=800&name=IMGP6697.jpg)

Hokosha Shrine

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMGP6717.jpg?width=800&name=IMGP6717.jpg)

Hinomikosha Shrine

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/togakushi-chusha.jpg?width=800&name=togakushi-chusha.jpg)

Chusha Shrine

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_2374.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_2374.jpg)

Kuzuryusha Shrine

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/Imported_Blog_Media/togakushi_13.jpg?width=800&name=togakushi_13.jpg)

Okusha Shrine

Next

- 1
- 2
- 3
- 4
- 5
- 6

Togakushi is home to five major shrines: the Hokosha, Hinomikosha, Chusha, Kuzuryusha and Okusha shrine. Each enshrines a deity connected to the Shinto legend of the sun goddess, Amaterasu. The Togakushi Kodo Trail connects each of these shrines, winding through sections of lush forest and passing weathered statues and moss-covered monuments along the way. Occasionally, the trees give way to views of Mt. Togakushi in the distance and idyllic hamlets surrounded by fields of buckwheat. On the final stretch to the Okusha Shrine, you are greeted by the striking Zuijinmon Gate and just beyond, towering rows of 400-year-old cedar trees.

Walking the full route covers approximately 14.5 kilometers and takes 6 to 7 hours (time for lunch included). There are bus stops for each shrine, so if you are short on time, you can start at the Hokosha Shrine or the Chusha Shrine and walk to the Okusha Shrine from there.

### Visit Kagami Pond that Reflects Mt. Togakushi in its Water

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_2323.jpg)

Kagami Pond is a picturesque body of water at the base of Mt. Togakushi, about 1.6 km from the Zuijinmon Gate of the Okusha Shrine through the Togakushi forest botanical garden (about 45 min. on foot).

On clear days, the rugged ridges of Mt. Togakushi are reflected on the still surface of the water. Nearby, you can stop and take a break at the charming log-built Donguri House, known for its gratins, tarts and desserts made with fresh local Nagano fruit.

In winter, the pond freezes over and becomes blanketed in deep snow. While the trail is completely obscured by the snow, the pond is still accessible via one of Togakushi’s marked snowshoeing courses (more below).

### Snowshoeing in Togakushi

Previous

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMGP3541.jpg?width=800&name=IMGP3541.jpg)

Torii gates buried in heavy snow

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMGP3545.jpg?width=800&name=IMGP3545.jpg)

The freedom of snowshoeing

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMGP6587.jpg?width=800&name=IMGP6587.jpg)

Mt. Togakushi in the background

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMGP6597.jpg?width=800&name=IMGP6597.jpg)

A statue buried in heavy snow

Next

- 1
- 2
- 3
- 4

The forests of Togakushi are perfect place for a snowshoeing stroll during winter. As long as you know where you’re headed, you can freely move around the snow unimpeded by bushes or small streams. There are several places that rent snowshoes during winter, including the Togakushi Tourism Association by the Chusha Shrine, the Okushamae Naosuke restaurant next to the entrance to the Okusha Shrine, as well as Togakushi Ski Resort.

There a several marked courses around Togakushi, and the most popular begins from the entrance to the Okusha Shrine. After about 20 to 30 minutes, you'll reach the Zuijinmon Gate and Togakushi’s lane of cedar for the area’s most striking views. The contrast of red against evergreen trees and pure white snow is stunning, accentuated by the height of these 400-year-old giants.

From the Zuijinmon Gate, follow the colored flags wrapped around the trees as you snowshoe through powdery snow on the way to Kagami Pond. Along the way, you may find some statues half-buried in the snow, as well as the vermillion torii gates of Tenmei Inari Shrine. From Kagami Pond, you can take in the views of the precipitous mountains of Togakushi.

\*The section beyond the lane of cedars to the Okusha Shrine is closed during winter.

### Hiking and Mountain Climbing in Togakushi

![IMGP7307](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMGP7307.jpg)Hiking through the forest

Togakushi and its surrounding area offer several day hikes accessible by bus. Just outside of Togakushi proper, Mt. Iizuna and Mt. Kurohime are both popular options for novice to intermediate hikers, while precipitous Mt. Togakushi offers a challenging climb with varied terrain for experience hikers.

At 1,917 meters, **Mt. Iizuna** has a variety of beginner-friendly courses and offers excellent scenery of the Togakushi mountains and the Northern Japanese Alps. The course from Ichinotorii Trailhead is easily accessible by Togakushi line bus. Take the Alpico Bus bound for Togakushi from Nagano Station and get off at the Iizuna Tozanguchi bus stop, then walk about 13 minutes to the south trailhead.

Slightly taller at 2,053 meters, **Mt. Kurohime** straddles the border of Togakushi and Shinano Town, overlooking Lake Nojiri. From the nearest bus stop (Togakushi Campground), walk 20 minutes along the road to the Ohashi Rindo trailhead. The full course takes about 6 hours.

**Mt. Togakushi** is a challenging hike reserved for skilled climbers. Sections of chains, narrow ridgelines and waterfall descents make it a thrilling but difficult experience. The Ari-no-To-Watari is the most harrowing portion, only as wide as one’s shoulders and dropping off steeply on both sides. Starting from the trailhead at the Okusha Shrine and finishing at the trailhead behind Togakushi Campgrounds, it takes about 7.5 hours from the Okusha bus stop (including the 40-minute walk to the Okusha Shrine and the return 55-minute walk from Togakushi Campground).

Before climbing mountains, be sure to prepare a mountain climbing itinerary to submit at the trailhead. [Learn more here.](https://db.go-nagano.net/en/climbing/)

### Make and Eat your Very Own Soba Noodles

Previous

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_6097.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_6097.jpg)

Cutting soba using a special soba knife

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_6137.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_6137.jpg)

Rows of freshly cut soba noodles

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_6242.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_6242.jpg)

Dipping the noodles into umami-rich soba tsuyu sauce

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_6308.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_6308.jpg)

The front of Togakushi Soba Museum Tonkururin

Next

- 1
- 2
- 3
- 4

Togakushi’s cold climate made rice farming difficult in the past, but it proved ideal for growing buckwheat. As a result, the area became famous for its soba fields and soba buckwheat noodles, shaping the local cuisine around these hearty noodles. Throughout Togakushi, you’ll find plenty of local restaurants serving zaru soba, chilled noodles served on a bamboo plate with a dipping sauce, as well as hot soba topped with fresh tempura. Soba tea is a natural complement to your meal. And if you’re not full yet, finish with soba dumplings or soba ice cream.

However, there is nothing better than eating your very own noodles. To do this, head to **Togakushi Soba Museum Tonkururin**, where a soba master guides you to making them from scratch. Here they lead you through each step, from mixing soba flour and water, to kneading and rolling the dough into a fine sheet before cutting it into noodles using a traditional soba knife. The slices may not be perfectly even, but that’s part of the charm. After the mini workout, the staff will cook your freshly made noodles and serve them up for you to enjoy.

### Explore Togakushi’s Ninja History

Previous

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_4079.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_4079.jpg)

Inside Togakushi Ninja Museum

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_4083.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_4083.jpg)

Displays of ninja tools and other paraphernalia

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_4101.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_4101.jpg)

The entrance to Togakushi Ninja Museum

Next

- 1
- 2
- 3

According to legend, the 12th century samurai warrior Daisuke Nishina combined samurai fighting styles with the mountain ascetic practices of Shugendo to form Togakure-ryu Ninjutsu, a form of ninja martial arts. The area became a haven for ninja spies, and there are several facilities around Togakushi where you can learn more about real ninja and their history. To see actual ninja tools, practice shuriken-throwing or escape from the Karakuriyashiki trick house, visit the **Togakushi Ninja Museum** across from the Okusha Shrine. If you’re traveling with kids, consider visiting the **Chibikko Ninja Village** to the right of the Togakushi Chusha Shrine. It is also possible to practice ninja martial arts as part of a private lesson. [Learn more here](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/id20024).

## Nearby Sightseeing

### Obuse Town

Previous

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMGP1252.jpg?width=800&name=IMGP1252.jpg)

Walking through central Obuse

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMGP1265.jpg?width=800&name=IMGP1265.jpg)

Obuse's narrow chestnut path behind merchant houses and sake breweries

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_2497.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_2497.jpg)

Inside Hokusai-kan Museum

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_2397.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_2397.jpg)

Katsushika Hokusai's painting of a phoenix at Gansho-in Temple

Next

- 1
- 2
- 3
- 4

Following the Chikuma River east from Nagano City is Obuse Town, famous for its chestnut themed cafes and chestnut wood-paved streets. The famous ukiyo-e artist Katsushika Hokusai, who created _The Great Wave off Kanagawa_, temporarily stayed here during his later years, and you can see exhibitions of his many works at the Hokusai-kan Museum or his large ceiling painting of a phoenix at nearby Gansho-in Temple.

### Zenkoji Temple

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_9818.jpg)Zenkoji Temple

Come back further down of the Togakushi area and visit Nagano City. Famous for its Buddhist temple, Zenkoji, it has historically been a major pilgrimage site for travelers walking the Nakasendo Road from Edo (modern-day Tokyo) to Kyoto. Zenkoji is said to be home to Japan’s first Buddhist statue, brought to Japan over 1,400 years ago.

### Matsushiro Town

Previous

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_4204.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_4204.jpg)

The main gate of Matsushiro Castle Ruins

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_4214.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_4214.jpg)

Inside Matsushiro Castle Ruins

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_4290.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_4290.jpg)

The Former Sanada Family Residence

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_4303.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_4303.jpg)

Zozan Shrine

Next

- 1
- 2
- 3
- 4

Explore a historic town that’s just a stone’s throw from Nagano City. A former castle town, its streets are lined with pristine samurai residences featuring picturesque gardens. Take a stroll around its historical sites, such as the ruins of Matsushiro Castle, the Matsushiro Military and Literary Academy, as well as the Chikago bunker from WWII.

## Where to Stay

Previous

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_6554.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_6554.jpg)

An altar inside Oyado Suwa temple lodge

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_6582.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_6582.jpg)

A pathway leading to Oyado Suwa's more premium accommodation option

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_6597.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_6597.jpg)

The snow-covered exterior of Oyado Suwa

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMG_8198.jpg?width=800&name=IMG_8198.jpg)

Inside one of the rooms

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMG_8196.jpg?width=800&name=IMG_8196.jpg)

A cozy modern Japanese room

Next

- 1
- 2
- 3
- 4
- 5

Most people will stay near Nagano Station, not within Togakushi itself; However, there are few temple lodges around Togakushi for those who would like to further experience the area. Temple lodges include Oyado Suwa and Oumeitei Tsuji. Another option is awai Togakushi, offering refined but minimalist spaces near the Chusha Shrine.

### Important Info (for green season)

[Click here for the timetable and details for winter season >](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/timetable/hakuba-nagano-winter-reserved?hsLang=en)

![ticketing-icon](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/images/icon/ticketing-icon.png?width=500&height=500&name=ticketing-icon.png)Ticketing

- You cannot reserve a seat or buy a ticket in advance, even one day prior. Boarding is on a first-come, first-served basis, and purchasing a ticket does not guarantee that you will be able to board your preferred service.
- Please purchase your ticket on the day of boarding, and then join the boarding queue.

- The bus ticket for the Nagano to Hakuba line that you purchased allows you to board any bus on the same day.

- If you are concerned that the bus might be full, please line up early.
- We add more buses during busy times. But if the bus becomes full, please board the next available bus.

![luggage-icon](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/images/icon/luggage-icon.png?width=500&height=500&name=luggage-icon.png)Luggage

- This bus has a luggage compartment where you can stow your suitcases. There are no restrictions on the number or size of items.

![timetable-icon](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/images/icon/timetable-icon.png?width=500&height=500&name=timetable-icon.png)Timetable Updates

- The timetable for the green season will be updated around mid-March.
- We apologize for any inconvenience. We cannot provide the exact release date for the timetable. The schedule will be posted on the timetable page once it has been confirmed.
- If the schedule for next year is not yet available, we kindly ask for your patience. Please refrain from inquiring about the release date, as we cannot offer additional details beyond what is provided on the timetable page.
- This bus service operates year-round, with only minor changes to the schedule compared to last year. Until the updated timetable is released, you may refer to last year's schedule as a guide.

![toilet-icon](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/hs-fs/hubfs/images/icon/toilet-icon.png?width=500&height=500&name=toilet-icon.png)Onboard Facilities

- This bus does not have a restroom onboard, and there are no restroom breaks during the journey.
- This bus is not equipped with a wheelchair lift or designated wheelchair space, so it cannot accommodate passengers who wish to remain in their wheelchair during the journey. Please fold your wheelchair and store it in the bus's luggage compartment. Kindly note that unfolded wheelchairs cannot be accepted.

Accessible using public buses running from Nagano Station, Togakushi and the surrounding Myoko-Togakushi National Park is quick and easy to get to. Home to some of the most important Shinto shrines in Japan, the area plays a role in the creation myths of Japan itself; while its relative seclusion and deep forests were the birthplace of the Togakure school of ninja.

Nestled within the larger Myoko-Togakushi Renzan National Park, Togakushi is a place of special importance and one that will tempt you to go a little slower and explore deeper as you move into the true heart of Japan. As a registered travel agent and [Nagano’s No.1-rated tour and charter operator](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/smr/nagano-city/how-to-get-to-togakushi/#Header6), we offer both group and private tours, ski and travel packages, accommodation, private charters and more! For further details, scroll to the bottom of the page. Let’s start with the obvious question:

### **Where is Togakushi?**

Togakushi is a heavily forested alpine area that takes its name from Mount Togakushi (1904m), which rises above the surrounding area and village. That area is quite a wide region covering many attractions but in order to get your bearings, let’s consider the centre of Togakushi to be the Togakushi Tourist Information Center. Located in the upper village, it is around 20KM / 40-minutes drive from [Nagano Station](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/?p=13523). Local bus services operate from Nagano Station to various points in Togakushi, taking 45 to 70-minutes depending on your exact destination. Togakushi village has an average elevation of around 1200 metres above sea level, blessing it with a cool climate through spring, summer and autumn, and very cold winter. Nestled within the larger [Myoko-Togakushi Renzan National Park](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/?p=55009), Togakushi covers a wide area and boasts some of Japan’s most important Shinto shrines, beautiful walking trails, abundant flora and fauna along with the nearest ski resort to Nagano Station, Togakushi Ski Resort.

#### **FROM NAGANO STATION** / approx. 45 to 60 minutes

Exit Nagano Station via the Zenkoji Exit and head left toward the main intersection with the large video screen on the building across the street. Cross the road, turn left again, and walk a short distance to the **Alpico Bus Stop No. 7** (pictured below), where buses bound for Togakushi depart.

![](https://www.snowmonkeyresorts.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/aplico-office-1024x768-2.jpg)

BESbswy

Several buses run to Togakushi throughout the day, but the No. 70 bus is the most convenient. This route runs between **Nagano Station** and **Togakushi Okusha Iriguchi**, stopping at all major shrines along the way.

The main points of interest that you can disembark at are:

**Togakushi-Hokosha** (Lower Shrine) – approx. 50 minutes

**Togakushi-Chusha** (Middle Shrine) – approx. 60 minutes

**Togakushi-Okusha Iriguchi** (Upper Shrine trailhead, including the giant cedar avenue) – approx. 65 minutes

Listen for the driver’s announcement as you approach each stop.

To ensure a safe and comfortable ride for all passengers, **seat reservations are encouraged** on this route. Even if you don’t reserve in advance, you may still be allowed to board **if seats are available**, but reservations guarantee a smoother boarding experience and save you from waiting in line.

- **Book your seat in advance online** (recommended)
- Pay your fare on board if not pre-reserved using **contactless-enabled VISA cards** or **cash**
- **Large luggage** can be stored in the bus’s trunk compartment
- **IC cards like SUICA or PASMO cannot be use** d

Please note:

- **Some stops are boarding-only or drop-off-only** — check the timetable carefully
- You **must board from the stop selected in your reservation** if you have made one. If you board from a different location, it may be treated as a **no-show**, and your seat could be reassigned. If needed, please cancel and rebook your reservation.

For local transportation **within Togakushi**, including travel between shrines, please use the **[Togakushi Shuttle Bus](https://visit-nagano.alpico.co.jp/timetable/togakushi-shuttlebus)**.

Located around 1200 metres above sea level, Togkaushi is nestled within the larger Myoko-Togakushi Renzan National Park. Among its multiple peaks Mount Hiuchi is the tallest at 2,462 metres above sea level while the park takes its names from the peaks of Mount Myoko and Mount Togakushi. Extending into Niigata and the ski resorts surrounding Mount Myoko, the national park is a destination to itself that can be enjoyed throughout the year.
